audit-everyday-mismatch.why: everyday board cells compared against their own linked product's per-unit - the only check that asks whether the number we PUBLISHED agrees with the page we LINKED to. Measured 2026-07-31: 2,582 checked, 0 uncomputable, 0 without a board per-unit, 5 findings. Board-derived like guards/4-factor (2,582 on the same board), so the same measured 0.10 band applies. THIS CHECK WAS AN ORPHAN until 2026-07-31 - it ran nowhere, so its own history starts here. Eligible counts only everyday cells we hold a link for, so the number does not swing when the board gains sale cells or linkless ones.

audit-ff-carry.why: RATCHET DELIBERATELY OFF - this denominator is INVERSE. It counts EMPTY Family Fare search terms re-probed against Freshop, so the number FALLS when the FF pull gets BETTER (fewer empty terms to re-probe). A ratchet here would fire at whoever fixed the thing it watches, which is worse than no watcher. Pinned by its own clean twin in test-auditors. BLIND still covers the case that matters for this check - it examining nothing at all - which is exactly where it sat on 2026-08-01.

audit-food-category.why: priced cells scanned for a wrong-CLASS product (the blueberries-as-Bai-beverage guard). Measured 2026-07-30: 2663 scanned of 3196 priced cells, 372 skipped because their commodity's category maps to no class list and 161 because the cell carries no product name. Board-derived, so the measured 0.10 band applies. A later same-day board rebuild read 2661 of 3194, well inside the band.

build-rescue-worklist.why: everyday walled-store board cells traced to a dated capture file. Measured on the first real run, 2026-07-31: 1,517 everyday cells across the four walled stores (Walmart 436, Sam's Club 347, Aldi 332, Fareway 402) and all 1,517 traced. Board-derived like guards/4-factor and audit-everyday-mismatch, so the same measured 0.10 band applies. Eligible is everyday cells of the four `walled: true` stores only - sale cells and the three headless stores stay out of the denominator, so the number does not swing on an ad cycle. Examined falls to 0 (BLIND, exit 3) if the capture files vanish from out\, which is the fresh-clone / cloud-runner state: every cell would read UNTRACEABLE and the emitted lists would be a full re-pull rather than a rescue. max_age_days 3 because it runs on the ad cycle, not on every publish.

guards/10-store-charges.why: Wide on purpose: the denominator is every priced row across all store feeds, so it steps whenever a walled store lands a big capture (24,018 -> 29,542 in three days). Narrowing it would cry wolf on a normal Walmart or Sams import. Revisit once coverage-ledger-history.jsonl holds a few weeks of per-check movement.

guards/11-bakers-provenance.why: Bakers is a full API pull, so this is normally flat (6,936 -> 6,947). The width covers a partial Kroger API run rather than day-to-day noise. A candidate for narrowing once history exists.

guards/3-pin-derivable.why: SMALL-N, where a percentage is the wrong instrument: the denominator is override pins (19 today, 1 pin = 5%), and pins collapsed 19 -> 1 in July when generate-board-overrides stopped minting one per same-day pull. A tight percentage here fires on ordinary pin churn, not on lost coverage.

guards/3-pin-identity.why: SMALL-N, same denominator as guards/3-pin-derivable. This is the row that sat at 0 of 16 while the ok line said 16, so BLIND is the verdict that matters for it, not REGRESSED.

guards/4-factor.why: board cells compared against their own linked product's per-unit. The single largest coverage number on the publish path and the one most directly tied to the board, so the measured 0.10 band applies.

guards/5-multipack.why: DEAD RATCHET until 2026-08-01: this was 1.0, which put the regression floor at 0 and made REGRESSED structurally unfirable. 0.5 is deliberately wide and the reason is measured, not guessed - this denominator is driven by how VERBOSE the Walmart capture is (guard 5 counts rows whose NAME states a pack count), and guards.ps1 records that it sat at 0 for every newest-Walmart file from 2026-07-05 to 07-14. A terser capture legitimately halves it; anything past half is the silent no-op guard 5 warns about.

guards/6-collapse.why: SMALL-N: 7 stores, so one store dropping out is -14%. 15% is the tightest band that does not fire when a single store has no capture history (sams today).

guards/9-freshness.why: SMALL-N: 7 stores, same arithmetic as guards/6-collapse.

pull-regular-hyvee.why: Hy-Vee products we hold a productId for that Aisles Online actually answered for. This is the first PULLER on the ledger rather than a check, and it is here because the pull's own numbers were being thrown away: check-ad-cycles piped it to Out-Null and logged an unconditional success line, so a truncated pull, a collapsed pull and a clean 1,010-product pull were identical in the log. Band measured off the retained history rather than guessed: refreshed_today sits at 1,006-1,065 on every file since 2026-07-19, and the worst day-over-day drop in that stable era is -8.1% (07-24, 1008 -> 926), so 0.15 gives ZERO findings on real history while still catching the wall-clock cap starting to bite. The -30.4% on 07-15 predates the stable era (the file went 448 -> 1,127 rows that week) and is not representative. Eligible is $refreshable, so the 485 products with no link at all - the no-discovery-path problem - correctly stay OUT of the denominator instead of making the pull look permanently broken. max_age_days 3 because it runs on the ad cycle, not on every publish.
